correctness.rationale: After detecting a false *auxiliary* assertion in original RESULT.md (distinct edge-disjoint squares can share two vertices), replaced the complete proof. Independent counterexample: squares x-a-y-b-x and x-y-c-d-x use eight disjoint edges but share x,y; no two have an edge in common. The repaired argument uses only |N(x)∩N(y)|≤2 and uniqueness of a square for each opposite pair. Original and filled double-cover cone covers have exactly the same nerve; all nonempty intersections are simplices. Every added disc has two valid free-face collapses per lift because original cycle edges and right-side diagonals are unique, yielding 2v vertices and 2e−2k old edges, same components, and ranks 2e−2v+1−2k or e−v+1−k per bipartite sheet. The corrected complete RESULT.md was written and audited before closeout.
